title: Reported history versus observed measurements
content: Reported history identifies an assertion attributed to a narrative source. An observed measurement identifies a supplied observation with its collection context. These labels describe how information entered a fictional record, not whether either source is correct. A note can contain both reported symptoms and copied measurements with separate attribution. Retrieval experiments can seek passages about separating history from observation. Repetition of a reported assertion does not convert it into a verified event. This research document concerns representation only and does not infer a condition from either type of entry. Synthetic research evidence only. Retrieval relevance != clinical validity.
